Definition: from G3844 and the base of G939; to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command:--(by) transgress(-ion).
BiblicalUsage: Parabainō is to go aside, to step over the line, to transgress. The Pharisees ask why the disciples transgress the tradition of the elders, Jesus asks why they transgress the commandment of God by their tradition, and Peter says Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word draws the line plainly. Men cross God's line to keep their own traditions, and Judas crossed it to his own place.
